analysis.investment_thesis: Blue Jet Healthcare sports the best ROCE in this batch at 57.3% — exceptional for any business globally — and is virtually debt-free, but current earnings yield of ~5.5% (Operating Income INR 406 Cr ÷ EV ~INR 7,319 Cr) sits just below the 6% threshold, and the OCF collapse to INR 46 Cr against net profit of INR 305 Cr in FY2025 demands explanation before committing capital.
key_strengths: ROCE of 57.3% is exceptional — high-value contrast media intermediates and niche API chemistry creates a near-irreplaceable position with global pharma customers
Virtually debt-free (D/E 0.02, finance cost effectively zero) — the entire earnings base belongs to equity holders with no interest tax
Revenue jumped 44% in FY2025 (INR 710 → 1,026 Cr) with operating income up 85% — suggests strong order-flow acceleration, not one-off
key_risks: OCF collapsed to INR 46 Cr in FY2025 despite net profit of INR 305 Cr — working capital absorbed ~INR 260 Cr in cash, likely large trade receivables from the revenue surge
FCF turned negative (-INR 34 Cr) in FY2025 as capex ran INR 80 Cr — the high ROCE is computed on current assets but capital is actively being deployed into capacity
Revenue was essentially flat (INR 538 → 710 Cr) for four years (FY2020–FY2024) before the FY2025 surge — concentration in contrast media creates lumpy, customer-dependent demand
red_flags: OCF/Net Profit ratio of ~15% in FY2025 (INR 46 Cr OCF vs INR 305 Cr net profit) — severe working capital deterioration that must normalize for the earnings quality argument to hold
FII ownership is only 0.89% — thin institutional coverage may mean pricing inefficiency exists in either direction
Capex has accelerated sharply (INR 23 Cr → 59 → 174 → 80 Cr) — if capacity build does not convert to revenue, ROCE will compress
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Blue Jet Healthcare is a niche specialty chemistry company manufacturing contrast media intermediates and pharmaceutical APIs — a segment with high technical barriers, long customer qualification cycles, and multi-year supply contracts with global innovators. These economics produce genuinely exceptional returns: 57.3% ROCE, 52.1% ROE, and 52.96% gross margins. For Greenblatt, the ROCE alone puts this firmly in top-decile territory. The company is virtually debt-free, so the entire EBIT flows to equity holders without leverage distortion.

The earnings yield of ~5.55% is the sole reason this is a HOLD rather than a BUY — it just misses the 6% threshold, and the current P/E of 52x makes it optically expensive. However, the forward P/E of 23.78x signals consensus expects a further earnings step-up, which would push forward earnings yield to ~8–9%, well into attractive territory. The critical near-term watch is the OCF collapse — if FY2025's INR 46 Cr OCF is a working capital timing issue (large quarter-end receivables from the 44% revenue surge), it will normalize. If it reflects structural cash conversion deterioration, the ROCE advantage is illusory. Watch FY2026 Q1–Q2 OCF closely before increasing position.
